prompt:
Isometric pixel art for a small isometric harbour-building game, in the tradition of classic isometric strategy and city-building games and modern isometric pixel illustrations. Strict 2:1 pixel isometric projection: every slanted edge steps exactly 2 pixels across for 1 pixel up or down, clean straight stair-stepped lines, no curved perspective. Crisp square pixels on one strict grid, every art pixel a solid 4 by 4 block of identical colour (the image is 384 by 256 art pixels shown at 4x), hard edges, no anti-aliasing, no blur, no soft gradients, no glow, no noise. Limited palette of about 40 muted dusk colours, 4 tones per material, light from the upper left: top faces lightest, left-facing walls medium, right-facing walls darkest. A one-pixel dark plum outline around every object. Hand-placed pixel detail like careful hand-made pixel art: rows of grey stone blocks with darker mortar lines on the cottage walls, rows of slate shingles on the roof, a stone chimney cap, wooden door planks, window frames with warm yellow panes; brick courses on the lighthouse plinth, a dark iron gallery railing, a red lantern roof; clinker planks and a white-red painted rim on the boat hulls, a small white wheelhouse; iron hoops on the barrel, nailed planks on the crates, twisted strands on the rope coil, an iron lantern frame on a wooden post. Not a 3D render, not a photograph, not a painting, no smooth shading.

The reference image is the exact layout and pixel grid: eight objects on a flat magenta background, already drawn in rough isometric pixel art from a 3D model. Repaint every object in place: same position, same size, same silhouette, same isometric angle, same pixel grid of 4 by 4 blocks and the same colour scheme (grey stone cottage with slate-blue roof, red shutters and lit windows; white lighthouse with one red band; white and red fishing boats with brown wooden decks; brown wooden barrel, crates and lantern post; pale rope). Add the hand-pixelled surface detail described above. Keep every object separate, with the magenta background between them. Lit windows and lamps are flat warm yellow panes, without any light beam, halo or glow (light is animated separately in the game). No smoke from the chimney. No ground, no water, no shadows under the objects.

The objects belong to this place: Location: the small harbour of Lornholm, a fictional island in a northern sea, at dusk. A stone quay with a short wooden jetty runs along the lower third of the picture. Two small wooden fishing boats are moored at the jetty. On a rocky headland on the right stands a white lighthouse with one red band, its lamp lit. On the left a small stone harbour-master's cottage with a lit window and a smoking chimney. On the quay: two barrels, a stack of crates, a coil of rope and an iron lantern on a wooden post. Calm sea, low clouds, a band of orange light at the horizon, the first stars.

Isolated on a fully transparent background. No text, letters, numbers, signatures, watermarks or logos anywhere in the image. No real places, brands, franchises or recognisable characters from existing games or films.

Image format: landscape 3:2.

Dialogue portrait for the side panel of an isometric pixel-art adventure game: head and shoulders of one character, 64 by 64 art pixels, every art pixel a solid 16 by 16 block of identical colour on one strict grid (the image is 64 by 64 art pixels shown at 16x). Hand-pixelled portrait technique: clean clusters, no single stray pixels, hard edges, no anti-aliasing, no blur, no soft gradients, no texture noise, no glow. Limited palette of about 28 muted colours with 4 to 5 hue-shifted tones per material (greens toward teal in the shadows, the red scarf toward crimson in the shadows and warm orange-red in the highlights, the dark fur from deep blue-grey to warm grey, the white fur warm cream), light from the upper left, a one-pixel dark plum outline around the figure. A readable, friendly face: the broad white stripe from the nose over the forehead, the dark stripes through the eyes, shiny dark eyes with a one-pixel highlight, a black nose tip at the end of the pointed snout, a small closed smile. Not a 3D render, not a photograph, not a painting.

The first reference image is the exact layout and pixel grid: a rough pixel-art portrait rendered from a 3D model, on a flat magenta background. Repaint it in place with the same framing, the same pose (three-quarter view, looking toward the left of the picture), the same size and the same 16 by 16 pixel blocks, and add the hand-pixelled detail: fur tufts at the cheeks and ears, the brass button and the brown band of the cap, knitted ribs of the scarf, the brown leather strap across the vest. The second reference shows the costume and the proportions of the character: take only the costume, the colours of the clothes and the face markings from it; drawing style, resolution and palette follow this description.

The badger courier: an original mascot character, a stout, short-legged badger with a broad black-and-white striped face, wearing a dark green peaked cap with a brass button, a dark green vest with pockets over a cream shirt with rolled-up sleeves, a long red knitted scarf, a brown leather satchel on a shoulder strap, and a brown paper parcel tied with string under one arm.

Isolated on a fully transparent background, no frame border, no background scenery. No text, letters, numbers, signatures, watermarks or logos anywhere in the image. No real places, brands, franchises or recognisable characters from existing games or films.

Image format: square 1:1.
